questions.prompt: At a point where ∇J = 0, what can you conclude?
options: It is a local minimum, as long as J is differentiable at the point
It is a stationary point: a minimum, maximum or saddle; check the curvature
The loss must be zero there, since the gradient vanishes at the point
It is a global minimum of J, since the slope is zero there
questions.explanation: Zero gradient only says the first-order change vanishes; J(x) = −x² has a stationary maximum.

questions.prompt: On J = (θ − 3)², why can a large step size increase the loss even though −∇J points downhill?
options: The gradient is computed wrongly whenever the step size alpha is large
The gradient changes sign after the step, so the update turns uphill
The first-order model is only valid locally, so a long step overshoots
Descent directions exist only for alpha < 0.1, so large steps go uphill
questions.explanation: The step moves past the valley floor; error multiplies by 1 − 2α, magnitude above 1 when α > 1.

questions.prompt: Which update performs gradient descent on J?
options: θ ← α∇J(θ) with α > 0, which replaces θ by the scaled gradient
θ ← θ + α∇J(θ) with α > 0, which follows the slope
θ ← θ − α/∇J(θ) with α > 0, which divides by the slope
θ ← θ − α∇J(θ) with α > 0, which steps against the gradient
questions.explanation: Adding the gradient climbs the loss; dividing by it is meaningless.

questions.prompt: For J = ½(λ₁θ₁² + λ₂θ₂²) with λ₂ ≫ λ₁, what limits the convergence speed of plain gradient descent?
options: The flat direction diverges first, which stops the iteration for good
Gradient descent converges in just two steps on any quadratic J
The gradient is exactly zero along the flat direction, so nothing moves
The step must be small for the stiff direction, so the flat one crawls
questions.explanation: α < 2/λ₂ for stability but the slow factor is 1 − αλ₁, close to 1.

questions.prompt: J = (θ − 5)², θ₀ = 1, α = 0.2. What is θ₁?
J(θ) = (θ − 5)² and one gradient step from θ₀ = 1 with α = 0.2 gives θ₁ = 2.6. What is J(θ₁)? Give 2 decimals.
J = ½(2θ₁² + 40θ₂²). What is the strict upper bound on α for stable gradient descent?

The error factor per step is 0.9. How many steps until the error is at most 1% of its start? (round up)
